evidence: The first loop runs once per element of a_list with O(1) map updates, but each element goes through ParseInt, whose cost is the token's length, so by the naming rule this is n strings each scanned once; the later d.Keys iteration is O(|d|). The tokens are numerals of at most 3 digits.

label: O(n+m)
what_to_look_for: The label O(n+m) implies two independent sizes, but the signature is (n, a_list) with n <= |a_list| and the statement gives A the same length N. evidence: The only loop runs i from 0 to n writing b[PyIndex(a_list[i] - 1, |b|)] and JoinInts(b) is linear in n; a_list holds exactly n values, so there is one size and the cost is O(n). The Python's `for i in range(N)` over A of length N is O(N) too, so the second variable m in O(n+m) names a size that does not exist.

evidence: The loop runs i from n-k to n, so k iterations (k is the x of the statement, 0 <= y < x < n), not n; each reads binary_list[i] in O(1). The cost is O(k) in a value, bounded above by the digit count n.
